title: Contract Pricing Agreement Reviewed Escalation: Notice Margin Reduction
content:
# Escalation notice margin and the reviewed escalation — Contract Pricing Agreement

**Rule.** The notice reduction follows the extra notice of the escalation, which is the calendar days from its notice date to its effective date, both as recorded on the escalation line, less the tier's escalation notice period. Calendar days from one date to another count the later date and not the earlier one.

| Extra notice | Reduction |
|---|---|
| 5 days or fewer | 0.5 percentage point |
| More than 5 and fewer than 30 days | 0.25 percentage point |
| 30 days or more | Nothing taken off |

**Tier escalation notice periods (calendar days).**

| Tier | Escalation notice |
|---|---|
| Corbett Account Price Schedule | 30 |
| Corbett Volume Discount Agreement | 30 |
| Corbett Category Contract | 30 |
| Corbett Net-Price Contract | 45 |
| Corbett Cost-Plus Contract | 60 |
| Corbett Strategic Supply Agreement | 60 |

The points are taken off the reviewed escalation allowance — the lesser of the reviewed escalation increase and the tier's annual escalation cap — before the escalation line's prior unit price is raised by it, and the allowance never falls below 0.

Hypothetical example: on a tier with a 45 day notice period, an escalation noticed 60 days before its effective date has 15 extra days and takes 0.25 point off; one noticed 48 days before has 3 extra days and takes 0.5 point off.
